petrol_car.source: UK BEIS 2023 — average medium petrol car
petrol_car.notes: Includes well-to-tank and tank-to-wheel emissions. For carpooling, divide by passenger count.

diesel_car.source: UK BEIS 2023 — average medium diesel car
diesel_car.notes: Diesel has lower CO2 per km but higher NOx. Divide by passengers for carpooling.

hybrid_car.notes: Combines electric and petrol drivetrain. Actual emissions vary with driving style.

ev.source: UK BEIS 2023 — battery electric vehicle (UK grid average)
ev.notes: Grid-dependent. Adjust by region using grid_factors. Includes manufacturing amortization.

bus.source: UK BEIS 2023 — average local bus (per passenger)
bus.notes: Per passenger-km. Varies with occupancy rate.

train.notes: Per passenger-km. Electric trains lower; diesel trains higher.

flight_short.notes: Includes radiative forcing multiplier. Short-haul defined as <3,700 km.

flight_long.notes: Includes radiative forcing multiplier. Long-haul >3,700 km. More fuel-efficient per km than short-haul.

walk_cycle.notes: Walking and cycling produce zero direct carbon emissions.

beef.notes: Includes land use change, feed, enteric fermentation, processing, and transport.

lamb.notes: High methane from enteric fermentation. Varies significantly by production system.

pork.notes: Lower than ruminant meats. Includes feed production and manure management.

chicken.notes: Lowest impact animal protein per serving. Dominated by feed production.

fish.notes: Varies widely: farmed salmon ~3.5, wild-caught whitefish ~1.0. Using weighted average.

eggs.notes: Per 2-egg serving. Includes feed, housing, and transport.

dairy.unit: kg CO2e per serving (~250ml milk equivalent)
dairy.notes: Covers milk, yogurt, cheese (normalized to milk equivalent). Cheese is ~3x higher per kg.

vegetarian_meal.source: Scarborough et al. 2014 — average vegetarian meal
vegetarian_meal.notes: Includes dairy and eggs but no meat. Typical meal with grains, vegetables, dairy.

vegan_meal.source: Scarborough et al. 2014 — average vegan meal
vegan_meal.notes: Plant-based only. Lowest per-meal footprint. Includes grains, legumes, vegetables.

IN.notes: India's grid is coal-heavy. Varies by state; southern states slightly lower.

IN-TG.notes: Telangana grid closely matches national average.

IN-KA.notes: Karnataka has significant hydro and solar capacity, lowering the grid factor.

IN-MH.notes: Maharashtra relies heavily on coal and gas thermal plants.

US.notes: US national average. Wide state variation from 0.05 (WA) to 0.8 (WV).

US-CA.notes: California has aggressive renewables targets, lower grid carbon intensity.

US-NY.notes: New York benefits from significant nuclear and hydro generation.

UK.notes: Declining rapidly due to offshore wind and nuclear. Was 0.5 in 2012.

EU.notes: EU average masks large differences. France: 0.052, Poland: 0.65.

NO.notes: Almost entirely hydroelectric. One of the cleanest grids in the world.

AU.notes: Still heavily reliant on coal, though rooftop solar is rapidly growing.

CA.notes: Canada benefits from extensive hydro. Provinces vary widely.

gas_heating.notes: Direct combustion of natural gas for space/water heating.

water.notes: Includes energy for treatment, pumping, and wastewater processing.

smartphone.unit: kg CO2e per device (amortized over 2 years)
smartphone.notes: Lifecycle emissions including manufacturing, transport, and use. Amortize: ~2.92 kg/month.

laptop.unit: kg CO2e per device (amortized over 3 years)
laptop.source: Dell Product Carbon Footprint / Circular Computing 2023
laptop.notes: Average laptop lifecycle. Amortize: ~8.33 kg/month. Refurbished saves ~70%.

clothing_new.source: WRAP UK 2023 — average new clothing item
clothing_new.notes: Weighted average across garment types. Fast fashion tends higher. Includes raw materials, manufacturing, transport.

clothing_secondhand.notes: Only transport and minor refurbishment. ~84% lower than new. Encourages circular economy.

metadata.notes: All factors are best-effort estimates from peer-reviewed or government sources. Real-world emissions vary by specific product, conditions, and behavior.
